verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents scoped OAuth access tokens: endpoints require specific scopes such as EVENT_TYPE_WRITE, and users can create OAuth clients. API keys can be managed in settings with test/live prefixes, and the MCP server uses an OAuth grant. However, the evidence shows scope enforcement on only one endpoint and nothing on scoping API keys or issuing per-agent least-privilege credentials. Missing for 10: a documented scope catalog, scoped or restricted API keys, per-agent credential issuance and revocation guidance, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: If accessed using an OAuth access token, the `EVENT_TYPE_WRITE` scope is required.
The Cal.com API has 3 authentication methods: 1. OAuth 2. API key 3. Platform (Deprecated)
You can view and manage your API keys in your settings page under the security tab in Cal.com.
When you first connect, your client walks you through an OAuth authorization flow where you grant the server access to your Cal.com account.
